newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian shares extend losses, down 4.93 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian shares extend losses, down 4.93 pct.

text.p: Brazilian stocks dropped 4.93 percent by mid-afternoon on falling U.S. stocks, a larger-than-expected July trade gap and a report that seven brokerages will be liquidated next week, brokers said.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index .BVSP of 47 most-traded shares was off 635 points at 12,237 points at 1442 local/1342 edt/1742 gmt on thin volume of 452.4 million reais ($417.7 million).
"It's a combination of factors that are depressing stocks but there's no liquidity so it is very easy to effect prices," a trader at local Sintese brokerage said.

Brokers said prices were sliding but fluctuating sharply due to the light turnover, including a steep drop in benchmark Telebras preferred, which fell 6.21 percent to 151 reais before climbing back some.
Telebras common plunged 6.39 percent to 139 reais.

Dealers said drops on Wall Street were behind the local decliners. But stocks extended losses on news of a larger-than-expected trade deficit of $811 million in July and a report the government plans to close several local financial institutions next week.
"The bolsa fell again a little while ago because of the report about the seven distribution houses and brokerages," one dealer said.
He was referring to a lunchtime report by O Globo television economics commentator Mirian Leitao, who said the houses were investigated by the Central Bank.
The bolsa's drop was led by electronics firm Sharp preferred, which nose-dived 7.5 percent to 1.11 reais.
Brokers also said some investors may have taken profits on Brazilian stocks, which were up 82 percent on the year when the market opened.
